title: 0.4% UPI fee on shop payments above ₹2,000 starts; traders push cash
body: From 15 October 2026, UPI payments to merchants above ₹2,000 carry a 0.4% merchant fee. It is capped at ₹300, which is reached at ₹75,000. Payments of ₹2,000 or less and person-to-person payments stay free. The page's example: on a ₹50,000 lehenga the fee is ₹200 plus ₹36 GST. Small vendors receiving up to ₹1 lakh a month keep zero fees. The government says merchants cannot pass the fee on as a surcharge. Traders' body CAIT has asked for a rethink, and the page says shopkeepers in Ghaziabad are considering refusing UPI from 15 October. A Chandni Chowk wedding-wear shop owner is cited as directly hit. This item is the page's account of shopkeeper reaction. Shopper reaction is not covered.

title: Dhanteras: gold and silver well below January peak, buyers go lightweight
body: On Dhanteras, 24-carat gold in Delhi (10 grams, including taxes) was Rs 1,48,800. That is down 19% from the record Rs 1,83,000 on January 29, 2026. Last year's Dhanteras price was Rs 1,32,400. Silver fell 52% to Rs 1,94,500 per kg from Rs 4,04,500, but is still above the Rs 1,70,000 seen on Dhanteras 2025. Jewellers said customers were mostly collecting pre-booked pieces. They expect volumes at par with last year or slightly higher. Buyers are favouring lightweight and 18K jewellery and other affordable items, because prices are still higher than a year ago.

title: Pune Dhanteras shoppers buy silver and light gold as rates hit nine-month low
body: Pune jewellers saw strong Dhanteras buying after prices dropped from their highs. One Kothrud jeweller said gold was at its lowest in nine months. His 24-carat gold was ₹1,41,000 per 10 g and silver ₹1,87,000 per kg. Silver was ₹3.8–4 lakh per kg in January. He said customers had been waiting for prices to fall and were buying 9- and 14-carat gold, temple jewellery, mangalsutras, silver idols and coins. Shoppers quoted on the page bought silver rings and anklets and small silver gifts. One said silver is now also seen as an investment.

title: Myntra and Flipkart lose festive fashion share as shoppers chase deeper discounts
body: Fynd's Festive Season Report 2026 says Myntra and Flipkart's combined share of festive fashion orders fell from 89% in 2025 to 76.8% in 2026. The report covers over 65 brands across eight marketplaces in September and October. Average festive discounts rose from 34% to 46%, and shoppers appear more willing to switch platforms for better deals. Orders above Rs 3,000 were 11.8% of transactions but over 41% of sales value. Tier II cities rose to about 35% of orders from 19% last year. Shoppers favoured affordable purchases amid household budget pressure, and Meesho is attracting price-sensitive shoppers.

title: Quick-commerce Diwali shoppers say extra fees inflate bills, care more about value than speed
body: A LocalCircles study found quick-commerce users shopping for Diwali rank best price or value first (71%) and product quality second (65%). Fast delivery came in at 22%. Low or no extra charges mattered to 43%. Six in 10 users say extra fees often make their final bill higher than expected, and on small orders even modest delivery or handling fees noticeably affect the total. Blinkit scored 5/5 for speed but 2.5 for value and charge transparency. 69% typically spend ₹200–₹999 per order. The study suggests many households are delaying purchases until closer to Diwali amid economic uncertainty.

title: Apple's Diwali ad 'Step Into the Light' panned on X as 'disconnected'
body: Apple's Diwali ad shows dancers with deadpan expressions doing unusual moves, including an Egyptian-style step, with a Juhi Chawla cameo and a 1990s Bollywood hit as the soundtrack. Users on X called it 'disconnected', 'depressing' and in some cases racist. One user said it captures how India looks more than how Diwali feels. Another wrote 'Representation is not the same as understanding'. Another said Apple 'really doesn't know India'. The article's author found the somber expressions odd for a festival of celebration.

title: Fewer seats, higher fares: flying home for Diwali costs more as IndiGo and Air India cut capacity
body: Airlines normally add festive seats, but this year they cut. Per OAG data, Air India's October seats were 3.3 million, down 12.6% (478,000 fewer). IndiGo was down 0.2% and SpiceJet down 38.8%. Akasa Air was the only airline to add capacity, up 35.6%. Fares on certain domestic routes have risen 'as much as 70%'. The article attributes this to high jet fuel prices, geopolitical challenges and rupee depreciation. The Centre told the Supreme Court that airfare-related rules under the Bharatiya Vayuyan Adhiniyam, 2024 would be published within two weeks. The next hearing is November 16. The page has no passenger quotes.

title: Airlines schedule 2.6% fewer domestic flights in November as high fares hit demand
body: The page, updated 2 November 2026, says Indian airlines scheduled 2.6% fewer weekly domestic flights for November. The figure is 22,306 against 22,912 in October 2025. It attributes the cut to higher airfares and 'signs of softer passenger demand', and cites Cirium data via Business Standard. Air India is down 14.9% (543 fewer weekly flights). Patna airport weekly departures fell from 377 to 302, and Hyderabad–Patna frequencies from 90 to 42. Smaller cities and routes popular with people travelling home are hit hardest. The article is inconsistent about whether the comparison is with October 2025 or October 2026.

title: ₹5 and ₹10 packs: shrinking grammage and 'magic price points' under pressure
body: Rising commodity, packaging, logistics and distribution costs are squeezing margins on ₹5 and ₹10 FMCG packs. Companies are cutting grammage, pushing larger packs as better value and nudging shoppers to higher price points. Britannia signalled 1.5–2% price adjustments in the September quarter, mainly through grammage cuts in ₹5 and ₹10 packs, which are 60–65% of its sales. A Maggi pack that cost ₹10 years ago now sells for ₹12–₹15. Some ₹5 chip packs fell from about 17 g to 8 g. An analyst says '₹10 will become the new ₹5' and warns that packs below about 20 g can leave consumers feeling cheated.

title: Ai+ smartphones raise prices by up to ₹3,000, advancing hike to November 11
body: Budget phone brand Ai+ moved its price hike from November 15 to November 11, 2026, citing stronger-than-expected demand and fresh stock bought at higher memory and component costs. Buyers can purchase at old prices until November 10. The Pulse 2 4+64 goes from Rs 8,999 to Rs 10,999, and the Nova 2 Neo 5G 4+128 from Rs 12,999 to Rs 15,999. The Nova 2 Ultra 5G 8+128 goes from Rs 19,999 to Rs 22,999. The NovaFlip 5G is unchanged at Rs 49,999. This is a syndicated press release that Outlook Business says is not independently verified. It carries no buyer reactions, but it shows the phone price rises hitting entry-level buyers.

title: Swiggy's Toing: ₹49–₹199 dishes, no platform fees, and a fight with Zomato's boss
body: Swiggy's budget app Toing, about a year old, prices dishes between ₹49 and ₹199 and operates in over 50 cities. Swiggy says two out of three new Toing users were new to food delivery. JP Morgan analysts reportedly said Toing may be poaching price-sensitive customers with lower menu prices, no platform fees and lower delivery fees. Swiggy's shareholder letter acknowledged it drew demand from the core app. Zomato founder Deepinder Goyal argued the lower-priced apps have not opened a new market. Fortune India estimated Toing's revenue at ₹500 crore and its losses at ₹400 crore. Swiggy's stock fell up to 15% after results.

title: MG raises Majestor, Hector Tomahawk EV and Windsor EV prices
body: MG India raised ex-showroom prices on three models. The Majestor rose Rs 1 lakh across all variants to Rs 43.49–45.99 lakh, its second hike in three months after a Rs 1.50 lakh rise in August. The Hector Tomahawk EV rose Rs 75,000 to Rs 20.25–24.25 lakh as its introductory pricing ended. The Windsor EV rose Rs 15,000 on the standard and Pro variants, to Rs 14.85–19.15 lakh. Battery-as-a-Service pricing stays at Rs 13.99 lakh plus Rs 4.90 per km. The page does not report buyer reactions.

title: ServiceNow launches another round of layoffs hitting India, UK and US
body: ServiceNow began another global round of layoffs that includes staff in India, the UK and the US. It has not said how many roles are going or which teams are hit. The company reported $87 million in severance and related costs for Q3 2026, against $24 million a year earlier. It says AI-driven efficiencies exceed $1 billion in annualised gains, and it aims to end 2026 with the same headcount it started with. CEO Bill McDermott called a smaller workforce a 'gorgeous situation' on the earnings call. That line is the kind of remark that stings employees. The page quotes no employee reactions.

title: Nearly 550 Innodata India staff reportedly lose jobs overnight
body: Nearly 550 employees at the US-based AI services firm Innodata's India operations reportedly lost their jobs on 26 October 2026. Innodata has not confirmed the figure. A termination email reviewed by India Today cited a reduction in the business assignment the staff were hired for, not individual performance. Workers said they lost access to laptops, email and internal systems during working hours, before formal notices arrived. Termination emails went to personal addresses. Affected staff formed WhatsApp groups to count colleagues. They are chasing pending salaries and final settlements.

title: Nasscom chief warns AI is squeezing India's IT freshers out
body: Nasscom president Rajesh Nambiar told Nikkei Asia that AI is automating entry-level coding and software testing, the work that has given freshers their first jobs. Nasscom projects about 6 million direct tech jobs in FY26, with a net addition of 135,000, up 2.3% year over year. Nambiar said: 'From a fresher's point of view, it is a concern, (and) I will not sugarcoat it any differently.' Nasscom is working with the UGC on a joint AI undergraduate curriculum that he expects to take about six months to approve. The page's editor notes that the lobby's own leader is effectively blaming freshers. The page reports no reactions from TCS, Infosys or the UGC.

title: Indian IT hiring in Q2: HCLTech adds 6,450 employees as Wipro loses 6,716
body: Headcount at big IT firms moved in different directions in the September quarter. HCLTech added 6,450 and took in 6,136 freshers, up from 1,056 in June. Infosys added 4,480, reaching 332,542, and TCS reached 598,056. Wipro fell from 243,044 to 236,328, a drop of 6,716. Voluntary attrition was 12.7% at Infosys and 13.8% at Wipro, and TCS called its 13.3% 'stable'. The page notes the firms define attrition differently. The page quotes only company executives, such as TCS's CHRO on upskilling. It quotes no employees.

title: India's IT job market is changing: what Q2 results mean for employees and freshers
body: Across six IT firms, the net addition in Q2 FY27 was 14,867 employees. Tech Mahindra added 5,446 and LTM added 949, while Wipro lost 6,716. The author argues that headcount growth no longer tracks revenue growth. Demand is rising for AI, data, cloud and cybersecurity skills, while traditional application development, testing and support roles need upskilling. Wipro onboarded about 1,000 freshers in H1 FY27, and its CHRO said campus hiring would resume in H2. The article has no employee surveys or quotes. Its view of what this means for freshers and mid-career staff is the author's interpretation.

title: White-collar hiring jumps 14% in October on Naukri JobSpeak, but IT lags
body: The Naukri JobSpeak index reached 2,836 in October, up from 2,480 a year earlier. That is 14% year on year, with auto up 36% and AI/ML roles up 32%. By experience, hiring for 0–3 years rose 15%, and for 13–15 years and 16+ years it rose 22%. Education fell 16%. Info Edge CEO Hitesh Oberoi said part of the jump reflects last year's festive-season base, and he called the hiring 'selective, fundamentals-led'. The page has no worker reactions.

title: Microsoft offers voluntary exit to eligible staff in India and three other countries
body: Microsoft announced a Voluntary Exit Offer for employees at level 70 and below in participating teams in India, the US, the UK and Canada. About 60,000 people are eligible globally, and Microsoft has about 23,000 staff in India. Indian staff have until December 1 to decide. Severance is reportedly one month's base salary per completed year of service, plus health insurance and career transition support. Chief People Officer Amy Coleman said: 'The Voluntary Exit Offer is new for us. We'll learn from it.' A CareerIndia piece dated 30 October says engineers are weighing stability against liquidity. It does not attribute that to named people.

title: Aon survey: salary hikes projected at 9.1% for 2027, but do raises beat inflation?
body: Aon's Salary Increase and Turnover Survey 2026-27 projects an average raise of 9.1% for 2027, up from 9% in 2026. Real wage growth is projected at 5.1% in 2027, against 4.3% in 2026. On a ₹10 lakh salary, the raise adds ₹91,000 before tax. The article warns that CTC is not take-home pay, because PF, gratuity, insurance and variable pay can sit inside CTC. It advises employees to compare revised monthly net pay and expected expenses rather than trusting the headline percentage.

title: CAQM orders 50% work from home in Delhi-NCR offices from Nov 5
body: The Commission for Air Quality Management ordered government and private offices in Delhi, Gurugram, Faridabad, Sonipat, Ghaziabad and Gautam Buddha Nagar to cap in-office staff at 50% from 5 to 20 November. The order is dated 30 October. Industrial units and essential services are exempt. Flying squads begin monitoring on 5 November, and violators face heavy fines. The Delhi government had already set a 50% WFH arrangement from 1 November. The article says HR and operations teams must sort out rostering, laptop logistics and attendance tracking before 5 November. It quotes no employee or employer reactions.

title: 'Going back to the campuses': Wipro headcount falls by 6,716
body: Wipro's headcount fell by 6,716 in Q2 FY27, a 2.8% sequential drop, to 2,36,328. The article calls it Wipro's biggest quarterly decline in recent quarters. CHRO Saurabh Govil said: 'We are going back to the campuses now in H2 to hire.' He added that AI-driven productivity is playing a role, that Wipro's salary increase took effect in March 2026, and that another hike is not under consideration. Net profit was down 1.4% year on year to ₹3,200.6 crore. The page quotes no employees.

title: Zoho's Sridhar Vembu: no pay increase this year, outlook for software jobs 'grim'
body: Zoho founder Sridhar Vembu told staff there will be no usual annual pay increase or appraisal review this year, and he apologised. He cited a 'massive 4-fold increase' in server prices, and said Zoho has not grown its headcount for 18 months. Zoho is still growing at 12%, but growth slowed more than expected in September. He said Zoho will try to avoid mass layoffs but called the outlook for software jobs 'grim'. He added that 'most of our employees understand the situation'. That is his own account, and the article reports no independent employee reaction.

title: Cognizant Q3: headcount 359,900, nearly 20,000 freshers hired this year
body: Cognizant's headcount stood at 359,900 at the end of September, up 3,200 in the quarter and 10,100 year over year. CEO Ravi Kumar S said nearly 20,000 fresh graduates had been hired this year, and that volumes are steady and moving further offshore. Net profit was $627 million, up from $274 million, helped by a lower tax provision. Revenue was $5,664 million, up 4.6%. The article gives no figure for India headcount. It reports no employee reactions.

title: Gujarat trader hands staff over ₹1 lakh cash each on a silver plate; Diwali bonus video goes viral
body: A video of a Surat textile trader giving his employees their Diwali bonus in cash went viral. Each of the 20 employees got over ₹1 lakh, laid out on a silver plate in notes of ₹10, ₹20, ₹50, ₹100, ₹200 and ₹500. Several employees were moved to tears. The page says the clip was widely shared, and many people praised how he chose to reward his staff before Diwali. It quotes no individual comments. An embedded Aaj Tak post calls the employees part of the trader's family.

title: Techie claims Apple India gives employees no Diwali sweets or gifts; netizens split
body: An X user, Amish Thaker, posted that Apple's India office offers staff no Diwali sweets or gifts. A user who says he is an Apple India engineer replied that he could 'confirm lol'. The page has no figures, and the claim is unverified. One reply asked why an American company would be expected to celebrate an Indian festival. Thaker answered that every American company he had worked for celebrated Diwali, Eid and New Year. Others joked about Apple's logo being 'half eaten'.

title: Deepinder Goyal answers doctors' backlash over his Temple wearable in a 10-point X post
body: Eternal founder Deepinder Goyal posted a 10-point clarification on X after doctors questioned whether his forehead-worn Temple device can measure blood flow in the brain. He says Temple is a fitness and AI device, 'not proven to diagnose or prevent any disease'. He expects Indian buyers to be no more than 1% of sales. He tells price critics to wait for user reviews and denies paying anyone to post supportive content. A related Storyboard18 commentary says he should 'stop defending Temple and start selling it', and notes the exchanges have turned personal.

title: Instagram's racy-content boom brings followers but not brand deals; creators move to paid Telegram
body: Sexualised Instagram content grows follower counts but rarely wins premium sponsorships, so some creators are moving to paid Telegram channels. The page uses a Rs 50,000 brand collaboration as its example of the trade-off. It also cites EY's projection that India's influencer marketing industry will reach Rs 3,375 crore by 2026. Saurabh Sankpal of Re. Awakening Collective says 'It wins on reach and loses on money'. He adds that a brand manager 'now has to imagine the screenshot, the FIR and the trending hashtag'. He thinks educators, astrologers, finance and fitness creators are better placed to sell subscriptions.

title: KlugKlug CEO: influencer market may top Rs 20,000 crore but brands are paying for fake reach
body: KlugKlug CEO Kalyan Kumar estimates India's influencer market at Rs 20,000 crore, a figure the article says is not independently verified. Other industry estimates it cites are Rs 3,500–4,000 crore. He says about two in three Indian influencers have more than 50% fake or inactive followers, based on KlugKlug's own analysis. He says agencies keep recycling 'the same list of 20,000 influencers', and that branded posts can draw much lower engagement than a creator's regular posts because audiences tire of promotions. Payment cycles of 60 or 90 days are also a sore point for creators.

title: Meta tests 'Features' for 90-minute Instagram videos; Indian creators told not to ditch YouTube
body: Instagram is testing a format called Features that allows horizontal videos up to 90 minutes. The test began with selected creators in Brazil and is expanding to a small US group, per TechCrunch. Adam Mosseri admitted 'I have been against doing long-form video on Instagram'. A Meta spokesperson said it is 'too early to share a long-term monetization model'. YouTube's Partner Programme gives eligible creators 55% of net ad revenue. The article's advice to Indian creators is not to assume access yet, to keep YouTube for full-length videos and use Reels for highlights.

title: Instagram to use AI to spot teens posing as adults; Meta expands age checks worldwide
body: Meta announced on November 9 that it is expanding AI-based age detection globally. Teens who enter an adult birth date may still get age-based restrictions. The page says 'millions' of Instagram users are affected and gives no exact count. It places the move against Meta's August settlements with US states, valued at up to $18 billion, over alleged teen harm. The article says effectiveness depends on how accurately the AI can tell teens from adults. It quotes no parents or experts.

title: Kunal Shah lays out WhatsApp's next priorities: bills, loans, bookings and AI
body: Kunal Shah became WhatsApp's global head in June 2026. In an X post he named three priorities: richer conversations (voice notes, groups, stickers, video), simpler transactions with financial and telecom partners, and AI that helps users avoid missing bookings. WhatsApp handles more than 100 billion messages and 2 billion calls a day, with over 3 billion users worldwide. He added that 'Your personal messages and calls stay end-to-end encrypted' and 'Trust takes years to earn and a moment to lose'. The page gives no launch dates or partner names and quotes no outside reactions.

title: Meta's Muse AI agent could cost up to ₹8,999 in India; users still have no official access
body: Pricing that surfaced for Meta's Muse AI agent ranges from ₹1,799 (Muse Power) to ₹8,999 (Maximum). The billing period is not specified. The app passed 10 million downloads within two months, but Indian users lack official access. Meta has not confirmed the India prices. An executive at a major Indian payment gateway denied working with Muse's developers on payments, which is why card payments don't work yet. The article also notes such agents can solve CAPTCHAs, so websites may need to rethink how they handle automated access.

title: Korean singer Aoora's Bhojpuri 'Lollipop Lagelu' at IIT Kanpur fest goes viral
body: South Korean singer Aoora, a Bigg Boss 17 wildcard in 2023, sang Pawan Singh's 2008 Bhojpuri hit 'Lollipop Lagelu' at IIT Kanpur's Antaragini 2026 festival. The clip spread online. One user wrote 'Craziness overloaded. Do more like this in Delhi too'. Another praised him for 'bringing people together through music'. Fans mainly praised his stage energy and asked for more shows around India.

title: Grandmother's reaction to Ramayana film goes viral as film earns Rs 112.90 crore in two days
body: A video of an elderly woman reacting while watching Ramayana, starring Ranbir Kapoor and Sai Pallavi, spread on X. Per Sacnilk, the film made Rs. 64.85 crore net on day one and Rs. 48.05 crore on day two, Rs. 112.90 crore in total. One user called the grandmother's expressions the 'real treasure' of the film, worth more than box-office earnings. Others said the Ram–Sita pairing would touch every family's heart.

title: Bhopal station video of man holding child in packed Diwali train rush sparks demands for better arrangements
body: A viral video from Bhopal Junction shows a man struggling to hold a child while boarding a jam-packed train in the Diwali rush. The page gives no statistics. Social media users tagged the Railway Minister and asked for better crowd management, more special trains and better facilities. They worried about the safety of children and the elderly. Some asked why railways can't prepare months ahead, since 'festival dates are known well ahead of time'.

title: 'Ramayana' Day 6 Box Office Collection: Nitesh Tiwari epic crosses ₹750 crore worldwide, ₹500 crore in India gross
body: The Week reports, citing Sacnilk, that Ramayana's total domestic gross through Day 6 was ₹501.8 crore as of 9 pm, which is ₹87.9 crore more than Day 5. The worldwide estimate is ₹761.8 crore and the net domestic collection over six days is ₹420.84 crore. Day 6 gross was ₹74.49 crore across 22,424 shows, with ₹62.51 crore from Hindi. The page lists a combined budget of ₹4,000 crore. It carries no audience comments, only the numbers, so it shows how big the Diwali rush was and not what people said.

title: Top 5 Indian Box Office Weekend (November 6-8) Collections Cross 250 Crore Net as Ramayana Leads with 69% Share
body: Sacnilk puts the top five films at ₹252.75 crore net for the Diwali weekend. Ramayana took ₹174.00 Cr (69% of that), Scene ₹63.15 Cr, Mookuthi Amman 2 ₹8.95 Cr, AK 47 ₹4.30 Cr and Jailer 2 ₹2.75 Cr. Ramayana and Scene together made up nearly 94% of the top five's business, so the market was very lopsided. The article notes that Scene grew on both Saturday and Sunday, unlike the usual front-loaded star release. Jailer 2 and AK 47 slipped mainly because they lost screens. The page's own totals for Ramayana conflict (₹238.85 Cr in the table, ₹440.45 Cr in a sidebar).

title: Scene Box Office Collection Day 5
body: Sacnilk's live estimate shows Scene's Day 5 India net at ₹12.85 Cr, down 40.0% from Day 4's ₹21.40 Cr. Five-day India net is ₹97.40 Cr, India gross ₹113.15 Cr and worldwide gross ₹174.40 Cr. Day 5 occupancy was 43.2%. The page says the figures are estimates and can differ from the producers' numbers. The weekend chart earlier showed it growing on Saturday and Sunday, so the weekday drop is what trade watchers are now debating.

title: 'Jailer 2' opens big at Kerala box office amidst strong backlash from Mohanlal fans
body: Jailer 2 made ₹12.50 crore in Kerala on opening day, the second-highest in the state's history after Empuraan (₹14 crore) and ahead of Leo (₹12 crore). The original Jailer made ₹5.90 crore there. India opening-day gross was ₹70.25 crore and domestic net ₹59.70 crore. Many Kerala fans of Mohanlal said they were disappointed by his limited role. His costume designer said three looks he created were cut and that he won't work on a Jailer 3. Fans online accused the makers of shrinking Mohanlal's part to keep the focus on Rajinikanth.

title: Jailer 2 Hindi Box Office: Rajinikanth Starrer To Miss The Hit Verdict?
body: Koimoi says Jailer 2's Hindi version has made ₹50.3 crore net (₹59.35 crore gross) after 24 days. That is ₹1.7 crore short of the ₹52 crore net needed for a Hit. Shows fell from 3,428 to 103 after Ramayana arrived. Weekly nets were ₹30.65 Cr, ₹13.15 Cr and ₹6.35 Cr. The film cost ₹26 crore and Koimoi puts its ROI at 93.46%, so it expects a Plus verdict. The takeaway is that a profitable film was squeezed out of cinemas by the Diwali mega-release.

title: Ramayana X review: Yash gets all love, Ranbir Kapoor gets flak
body: On opening day, viewers' posts on X were split. Yash's Ravana was the favourite, with the Jatayu vs Ravana sequence called thrilling, and one IMAX viewer said it left them speechless. Some found Ranbir Kapoor's Rama dull and questioned Sai Pallavi's casting, and others objected to a fight scene involving Sita that is not in the original epic. Complaints included slow pacing, a long runtime and weak music, and one reviewer gave 1.5/5, 'Strictly for Yash'. One viewer called it 'EPIC SCALE, MIXED EXECUTION', and another said the Hindi original works better than the 30-minute-shorter English dub.

title: Ramayana Music Draws Divided Reactions but Has A.R. Rahman and Hans Zimmer's Collaboration Lived Up to Expectations?
body: Sacnilk says the Ramayana soundtrack became 'a subject of disagreement rather than universal celebration'. Some listeners felt 'Mangal Rang' (Arijit Singh, Shreya Ghoshal) drifted from the devotional tone, and 'Ravana Tandav' was questioned for its electronic sound. Even so, 'Mangal Rang' reached the top of YouTube's trending music chart. After release, some viewers felt the orchestral style suited a Hollywood spectacle more than an Indian devotional story, while the Jatayu action score was praised. Rahman said the work was about ten films' worth and went through extensive revisions.

title: Mookuthi Amman 2 X Review: Nayanthara's film gets strong reactions, fans call it 'paisa vasool'
body: Navbharat Live says reactions on X were mostly positive for Mookuthi Amman 2, which released on 6 November. Viewers praised Nayanthara's screen presence and Hiphop Tamizha's background score, and called Sundar C's simple storytelling suitable for all ages. Some users said forced comedy, weak CGI and a slow narrative held it back. The Sacnilk weekend chart shows it third at ₹8.95 Cr net, far behind Ramayana and Scene. The picture is of a festival family film with fans, but small in numbers.

title: Akka review: Radhika Apte, Keerthy Suresh rule the screen, but series falls short
body: The Federal reviews Netflix's five-episode series Akka, set in the fictional women-ruled kingdom of Pernuru. It praises Keerthy Suresh and Radhika Apte and calls their dynamic the strongest reason to watch. It says the series is only 'a gender-swapped gangster drama' with 'the personality of cardboard'. It blames choppy pacing on reported reshoots and cut gore, and says the ending rushes a promising caste-oppression thread. Other outlets in my search results also gave it mixed-to-negative reviews. I found no viewing numbers or audience ratings.

title: Diljit Dosanjh not allowed to sing 4 songs in Indore concert
body: Indore's District Child Protection Officer asked the venue, C-21 Mall, in a letter dated 6 November not to let Diljit perform four songs at his 15 November show: Patiala Peg, 5 Taara Theeke, Jeb Vicho Feem Labhi Aa, and Jatt Uthe Fire Karda Jithe Pabandi Hathiyara Di. He cited a July 2019 Punjab and Haryana High Court order against songs glorifying liquor, drugs and violence. A Chandigarh professor had complained and also raised concerns about children on stage, bullet-belt costumes, loud sound and flashing lights. The concert admits children aged five and above. Three private schools and the mayor's office received bomb-threat emails. The article has no response from Diljit or the organisers.

title: India vs West Indies T20I series ends 2-2 after Bengaluru washout
body: The five-match T20I series (27 September to 17 October) ended 2-2 when rain abandoned the decider at Bengaluru's Chinnaswamy Stadium. India were 118/5 in 7.4 overs, with Ishan Kishan scoring 30 off 10 balls, and West Indies' revised target was 84 in five overs. West Indies hit 105 sixes in the series at a run rate of 10.98. A sold-out decider ending in a washout was the main disappointment. The page itself has no fan comments.

title: From Bowling Concerns To Naman Dhir's Emergence: Five Takeaways For India As West Indies T20I Series Concludes
body: Outlook's takeaways (published 18 October, updated 10 November) say India's bowlers took 23 wickets, conceded 865 runs and had an economy rate of 11.13. India conceded 200-plus totals in three of the four innings they bowled, and in the second T20I failed to defend 248. Shreyas Iyer led the batting with 181 runs, including a century. Sanju Samson made 168 runs at a strike rate of 195.34. Debutant Naman Dhir took five wickets and ended unbeaten on 24 off 6 balls. Bhuvneshwar Kumar returned after four years. The article has no fan opinion, but the bowling worries are the main talking point.

title: Urban India heads into Diwali with a smaller wallet
body: Upstox Originals, citing a LocalCircles survey, says urban festive spending is expected at ₹1.97 lakh crore, down 6% from ₹2.10 lakh crore in 2025. The average household budget is about ₹20,000 and 31% of households plan no discretionary festive purchase. No-cost EMIs on Amazon rose to about 50% of purchases from 30% a year earlier, and 83% of households planning purchases expect to use savings. Gold in Mumbai went from about ₹93,000 to roughly ₹1.5 lakh per 10 grams between April 2025 and October 2026, and September retail inflation was 5.54%. The article says households still want to celebrate but are "checking the price tag a little more closely", and spending is "being counted more carefully before it leaves the wallet".

title: Diwali 2026: Indians set to spend $16 billion online as festive sales jump 25%
body: Business Today, citing a Bloomberg report that quotes Redseer, says online festive sales are projected at $16 billion (about ₹1.4 lakh crore). The 25% growth would be the fastest in five years. Diwali fell on November 8, 2026. Premium gifts are part of the story: Khoya's Gold Pista Katli costs ₹21,000 for 30 pieces, a Tanishq 2-gram 24-karat Lakshmi-Ganesha coin costs ₹31,702, and a Jaipur Rugs rug costs ₹3,45,450. The $16 billion covers the whole festive run-up, not Diwali day alone. The page quotes no shoppers. Read it next to the Upstox piece, which reports smaller baskets and more EMI use.

title: Dhanteras 2026: CAIT expects ₹1 lakh crore in festive trade, gold and silver projected at ₹66,000 crore
body: CAIT expects total Dhanteras business across all retail categories to cross ₹1 lakh crore. The jewellers' federation AIJGF projects gold and silver trading at ₹66,000 crore, up 10% year on year. The page says "overall spending enthusiasm remains entirely unabated", while consumers are "recalibrating their buying choices toward value-optimised items". The main buying window ran from 10:30 AM on November 6 to 6:37 AM on November 7. These are trade-body projections, not audited sales.

title: Gold sales reach ₹60,000 crore on Dhanteras as buyers shift to lightweight jewellery and smaller coins
body: Kotak Neo reports gold sales of about ₹60,000 crore, up 15-20% year on year, and combined gold and silver sales above ₹66,000 crore. Delhi 24-carat gold was ₹1.46 lakh per 10 grams on 6 November, against a January 2026 peak of ₹1.83 lakh and ₹1.32 lakh last Dhanteras. Silver was ₹1.92 lakh per kg, against a January peak of ₹4.04 lakh. The article says higher prices keep gold quantity roughly flat, buyers "increasingly opted for lightweight pendants, bangles and chains", and digital gold attracted younger consumers. Showroom visits and prior bookings were ahead of last year, especially in the west and north.

title: Mumbai bans rockets and aerial firecrackers till Nov 25 after Diwali fire calls
body: The BMC issued a prohibitory order on November 9 banning rockets and aerial firecrackers until 11:59 pm on November 25, 2026. It covers residential buildings, terraces, balconies and slum settlements. Penalties under the Disaster Management Act go up to six months in jail, a fine, or both. The Mumbai Fire Brigade got 142 fire calls on November 8, and 137 were linked to firecrackers. Fires were still reported across the city after the order, including Andheri, Kandivali and Dadar. The BMC says aerial crackers land on rooftops and balconies and set fires in dense neighbourhoods. Residents are being urged to "celebrate responsibly".

title: Gurugram bans construction till Nov 20 and orders 50% work from home
body: Gurugram's administration banned dust-generating construction and demolition across the district from November 5 to 20, 2026, following CAQM directions. Government and private offices must cap in-office attendance at 50%, with the rest working from home. Employers must prepare rosters and keep attendance records. Magistrates and pollution board officials will inspect daily, and non-compliant firms face action under the CAQM Act, 2021. Dr Randeep Guleria of Medanta warned that people with chronic lung or heart conditions, children and older adults are most vulnerable at severe AQI levels. The page quotes no employees.

title: Delhi-NCR 50% work-from-home order: seven things to know
body: Open Magazine (last updated October 31, 2026) explains the CAQM order dated October 30. State government and private offices in Delhi and five districts (Gurugram, Faridabad, Sonipat, Ghaziabad, Gautam Buddha Nagar) are capped at 50% in-person attendance from November 5 to 20. Railways, Metro, airports, hospitals, water supply, sanitation and industrial establishments needing on-site work are exempt. Construction curbs cover the whole NCR, including road, flyover and pipeline work. CAQM justified it using November AQI data from 2018 to 2025, which showed recurring Severe days. The page carries no worker or employer reactions.

title: November 1 rule changes: pension life certificates, ITR deadline, GST and LPG
body: IBTimes India (October 30, 2026) lists what changes in November. Pensioners under 80 can submit their Jeevan Pramaan life certificate from November 1 to 30, and late submission can temporarily stop pension payments. The ITR deadline for specified audited taxpayers moved from October 31 to November 21, but salaried individuals outside those categories are not covered. No LPG price change had been announced as of October 29, since oil companies revise prices monthly. The Cabinet approved a proposal to lower the disability pension threshold from 80% to 40%, with assistance of Rs 375 a month for those under 80 and Rs 625 for those 80 and above. It is not expected to start on November 1. The page quotes no public reaction.

title: India delays 0.4% UPI merchant fee after retailer pushback
body: TechCrunch reports that the planned 0.4% fee on eligible UPI merchant transactions above ₹2,000 was postponed from October 15 with no new date. NPCI cited the festive shopping season. Payments of ₹2,000 or less and merchants receiving under ₹100,000 a month via UPI are exempt, and the fee is capped at ₹300. UPI handled 24.07 billion transactions worth ₹29.37 trillion in September. Retailers and petrol pump operators opposed the fee, and some warned they could stop accepting UPI. Banks and payment firms say they need a way to cover UPI's running costs, estimated at about ₹200 billion a year.

title: NPCI revises UPI dispute rules: 'Wrong Payment' reversal requests from Nov 25
body: NPCI issued a circular on November 4, 2026 (NPCI/UPI/OC No. 240/2026–27) revising how UPI disputes are handled in the URCS system. "Wrong Credit Chargeback" is renamed "Wrong Payment – Reversal Request". New reason codes cover excess charges, duplicate transactions, cancelled or returned goods, and defective or undelivered goods or services. Evidence such as receipts, invoices or FIR/NCRP copies may be needed, depending on the dispute category. The rules take effect on November 25, 2026. This is a regulatory notice with no public reaction quoted, but it matters to anyone who pays the wrong person or is overcharged on UPI.

title: Navratri 2026 vehicle retail: 11.23 lakh units, down 6.52% on 2025, EVs near 10.5%
body: FADA's Navratri data (October 11-20, 2026) shows 11,23,086 vehicles retailed. That is up 26.76% on 2024 but down 6.52% on 2025. Two-wheelers were 8,34,075 units and passenger vehicles 1,82,728, down 21.91% on 2025. EVs made up about 10.46% of registrations, against 7.71% a year earlier. FADA President Sai Giridhar said the drop against 2025 was "primarily influenced by calendar differences", since Navratri 2025 ran 11 days and GST 2.0 pulled demand into it. This is dealer-body data, not buyer commentary.

title: Startups are now selling the meet-up as adults pay to make friends
body: Open Magazine (last updated October 22, 2026) says startups are turning in-person socialising into a paid product, from hobby clubs to organised meet-ups. It names Misfits, a Gurugram hobby-community startup founded in 2022 that raised ₹5 crore in seed funding. It cites Eventbrite's 2026 Social Study for growth in things like puzzle competitions and flower arranging, but gives no figures, and notes the data covers only Eventbrite's own marketplace. The article's central point is that "the challenge is keeping customers coming back once strangers become friends". The page quotes no founders or customers.
